schedule.rule: recurrent_depth.schedule_from_spans(layer_merge.spans_from_kept_blocks(36, kept_blocks)): logical layer p runs block layer_to_block[p] and stands where root block root_layer_of_layer[p] stood; block j runs |S_j| times in a row
schedule.what_an_iteration_is: a whole decoder block -- input RMSNorm, attention with q/k norm and RoPE, residual add, post-attention RMSNorm, gated FFN, residual add -- with the block's shared parameters; each iteration's input is the previous iteration's output; the same token keeps its position id at every iteration; each logical layer has its own KV-cache entry
schedule.gradients: through every iteration: the 16 blocks are registered once with the optimizer and each parameter's gradient is the sum over its calls
schedule.config: configs/stages/stage-1/depth_recurrence/recurrent_config.json: the base's config.json (both paths share it: SOB1's depth init and variant 1's build both save it) with num_hidden_layers 36, layer_to_block, num_parameter_blocks 16, model_type aad_recurrent_depth (recurrent_depth.recurrent_config_from); the weight file is the base's, byte for byte
schedule.identity: a recurrent initialization's identity is its weights AND this config (the schedule): the same weights on another schedule are another model; its init record binds both (schedule.py init-record)

hidden_state.applies_to: DMR1-RH only; DMR1-R has no hidden-state term and runs the trainer's unchanged path
hidden_state.pairs: every logical layer p with the teacher layer root_layer_of_layer[p] (here p itself): 36 pairs, [[p, p] for p in 0..35]
hidden_state.what_is_compared: the student's residual stream after logical layer p (the raw output of the whole block call) against the teacher's after its layer p (the raw output of its decoder block); both before any final norm. The last logical layer's raw output is compared with the teacher layer 35's raw output; the final RMSNorm's output is not a hidden-state target and reaches the loss only through the head (CE / KD)
hidden_state.every_iteration: every iteration of a looped block is supervised, the first included: block j's first call against teacher layer j, its k-th against teacher layer j + k - 1
hidden_state.single_execution_blocks: INCLUDED (blocks 0, 4, 5, 6, 18, 22, 23): a block run once is the one-iteration case of the same rule, and the first iteration of every looped block is supervised the same way; excluding them would treat structurally identical calls differently. The alternative (supervise only iterations 2..|S_j|) is not registered
hidden_state.rows: the KD rows: the assistant prediction positions (kd_scope 'assistant'), row t being the position whose state predicts token t + 1 -- the same rows, with no further offset, whose final states reach the head for KD. Prompt and padding positions carry no hidden-state term
hidden_state.error: relative_squared_error_v1: per (pair, row) ||s - h||^2 / ||h||^2, the squared error of the whole 2,560-dimensional state divided by the teacher target's own energy at that row. This is a per-position RELATIVE squared error, not ordinary MSE: MSE would average the raw squared difference over the hidden width and rows, so its scale would follow the residual stream's norm at each depth and position; here every (row, layer) term is normalized by that row's target energy. Dimensionless, the width cancels, NOT bounded above (a student state larger than the teacher's gives values above 1)
hidden_state.normalization: the step's sum over pairs and rows divided by (36 pairs x the step's KD rows), the same row count that normalizes KD: a mean over layers, iterations and rows. The per-row denominator keeps a few very-high-norm positions (the residual stream's massive activations) and the deeper layers' larger norms from dominating
hidden_state.lambda_rationale: 1.0 is a PROPOSAL, not tuned and not validated (no search, no eval-set-1 reading); 0.25 is an alternative a reviewer may prefer, equally unvalidated, and neither is registered as 'KD-dominant'. What is measured is only the scalar size at step 0, at $0 on the KEPT recurrent init (logs/stages/stage-1/depth_recurrence/plans/step0_diagnostic_20261126.json: 2 validation sequences, 2,048 tokens, CPU): L_hidden 14.56 against KD 12.30, the term concentrated in logical layers 14-28 (block 7's six iterations and after). Three things this does NOT establish: (1) a loss value of similar size does not mean a gradient contribution of similar size -- the per-parameter gradients of the hidden term and of KD were not measured, and they reach the blocks through different paths (every logical layer's output vs the head only); (2) the global gradient-norm clip at 1.0 rescales the summed gradient as a whole, so it neither guarantees that KD dominates the update nor changes the two terms' relative share; (3) the clip bounds the gradient's norm, not the parameter update: AdamW normalizes each coordinate by its running second moment, so the update size is set by the learning rate and those moments, not directly by the clip. SOB1's depth KD fell from 3.54 to 0.41 over recovery; whether the hidden term falls with it is what the run's per-layer log shows. Measuring the two terms' gradient norms at step 0 on a GPU is a cheap addition to variant 3's engine validation; no lambda search is part of this round
hidden_state.teacher_side: the teacher runs the same packed ids without position ids (cross_context) under no_grad; its layer outputs are taken at the KD rows by forward hooks in the same forward its KD sketch comes from, each layer required to run once; they are targets only, never the student's inputs
hidden_state.student_side: the student's states are handed over by its own logical-layer loop (RecurrentDepthModel.forward(hidden_supervision=...)), outside the checkpointed block calls, so a recomputation never registers a loss twice; no detach between iterations
hidden_state.memory: the teacher targets at the KD rows in bf16: 36 x rows x 2,560 x 2 B (about 0.33 GB at the median 1,790 rows of one 8,192-token sequence, 1.5 GB at a full sequence); the error function keeps a reference to the student state the next checkpoint holds anyway, never a gathered copy

training.recipe: every other field of SOB1's depth unit, compared field by field (`plan.py`): stage stage3_recovery; seeds 20260726 and 20260801 in that order; 9,701 optimizer steps, 3 epochs of 6,467 packed sequences of 8,192 tokens; batch size 2, micro-batch size 1, 2 gradient accumulation steps; fp32 parameters with bf16 autocast and gradient checkpointing; the teacher in bf16 as the online KD teacher; CE 0.25 + KD 1.0, temperature 1.0, assistant scope, Top-200 + tail; AdamW lr 5e-5, weight decay 0.01, betas (0.9, 0.95), eps 1e-8, clip 1.0; 485 warmup steps, cosine to 0.1; the same trainable patterns (embedding / tied head frozen); cross_context packing (sequential, truncation allowed, standard causal attention); the same pack, tokenizer and save points (every 1,104 steps, keep 1)

after_packing.note: supervised-token exposure is counted from the trainer's log (sum of kd_positions), never derived

training.same_data_and_steps: the same pack, proportions, order (the trainer's per-epoch permutation from the seed), 9,701 optimizer steps and pre-packing token budget as the single-execution control: recurrence deepens the computation per token, it adds no training token; the loop arms are NOT shortened to match FLOPs
training.independent_runs: each loop arm trains from its own training-pre initialization, independently: never from a recovered final (SOB1's or V1's) and never from the other loop arm's weights

unit_order.rule: both conditions run; neither is cancelled because the other finished first or trails a baseline (maintainer principle 16): one session per arm, V2-D first (the first session carries the engine validation), V2-M second; then stop for review

durability.basis: TPI1's 20 save points and finals: uploads 121-161 MB/s; verifying downloads 128-386 MB/s, with an episode of 2.6-4.6 MB/s on the private-repo download path (2026-11-17/18). A 2B save point is 20.9-22.6 GB, so a floor-rate verify takes up to 2.4 h: copies get their time from their bytes, and a session stops training early enough to secure its last save point and the final before its hard deadline

weights uploaded and verified are never sent again: only their record's publication (the handoff) is retried (SavepointMirror.mirror_once, hand_off_with_retries)

analysis.effect_interval: per comparison, the percentile 95% group-bootstrap interval: the 558 independence groups resampled with replacement, the estimate sum_g d_g / sum_g n_g with d_g the group's summed item contrasts, 10,000 resamples, numpy default_rng(20261120). R4 resamples groups with all four conditions' records of each item together, so its interval keeps their pairing
analysis.family: no family and no error rate: descriptive single-seed estimates with item-sampling intervals
analysis.verdicts: none this round: each comparison is reported as an estimate with its interval
analysis.completeness: a comparison is read in a mode only when every condition it names covers all 570 items in that mode at seed 20260726; otherwise it is reported as not computed
analysis.seeds_and_items: one training seed: the intervals measure item sampling with each checkpoint fixed, not training randomness; no claim about another seed is made
secondary_descriptive: per reasoning axis (deduction, induction, composition, the abstract / analogical sub-category)
terminations apart from correctness: natural, degeneration stop, context-limit hit (right-censored length), usable rollout, mean generated tokens
validation CE / KD curves; for depth_loop_hidden the hidden-state error per logical layer (diagnostics, never a reasoning result and never a reason to drop a run)
compute: training FLOPs per token, seconds per step, peak memory, evaluation time and decode throughput (compute_accounting)
analysis.exposure: eval-set-1 is development-exposed: nothing here is a never-seen blind result
analysis.nothing_eliminates: no initial KL, CE, hidden error or generation score stops or drops a unit
analysis.target: the research target is inferring rules and abstractions from the information a task supplies and generalizing them (AGENTS.md P10.2); a lower diagnostic loss is never reported as a reasoning gain
analysis.selection_conditioning: both initializations are run, so nothing is selected on these items; the M - D single-execution difference that motivated the round was read on the same items (DMR1_REVIEW.md section 00)
analysis.interpretation: results are read as the four directly comparable differences. If the two recurrent conditions come out close, the merge's deficit is smaller under recurrence -- not that the merged initialization is better; the absolute accuracies are read beside it. This round cannot separate 'the weighting damaged the representation' from 'the training recipe suits it less': recurrence also changes the computation graph, the state distribution and gradient propagation. No mechanism is concluded here; whether variant 3 tests hidden-state supervision is decided after these results
analysis.no_rule_changes: the primary metric, the comparisons and the reading are fixed here; none is changed after a result

compute_accounting.training_forward_equivalents_per_token: teacher 36 layer forwards + student 4 per logical layer under gradient checkpointing (forward, recomputation, backward 2x): single 36 + 64 = 100, recurrent 36 + 144 = 180 (1.8x)
compute_accounting.inference: decode work and KV cache per token scale with the logical layers: 36 / 16 = 2.25x the depth arm's (the teacher's 36 layers' KV size, 147,456 B per token in bf16)
compute_accounting.reported: measured seconds per step, peak allocated / reserved memory of the first four steps, evaluation minutes and generated tokens, beside the comparison; the comparison is not FLOPs- or latency-matched
compute_accounting.matched: the same training data, proportions, order and optimizer steps as the single-execution controls: NOT the same compute. Reported: measured GPU hours, seconds per step, peak memory, evaluation time and generated tokens; 'same token budget' is never written as 'same compute'

step0_diagnostic.scope: 2 validation sequences truncated to 2,048 tokens on the dev box's CPU, the untrained KEPT recurrent init: evidence that THIS initialization starts degenerate on the 36-layer schedule (val CE 12.46, above the uniform 11.93; the single-execution base 3.46 on the same rows), nothing more. models.recurrent: the staged depth_loop_kept init (SOB1's depth weights + recurrent_config.json, 36 logical layers)
models.control: the same weights as a stock 16-layer Qwen3 (base_config.json): the bf16 noise floor of each engine path, measured in the same session

engine_validation.inputs: the first 4 validation sequences of the training pack, their first 384 tokens as prompts; 64 greedy continuation tokens each

checks.hf_cache: HF, bf16 on the GPU: logits of incremental decoding with the cache vs one full no-cache forward over the same tokens (the last 64 positions); the recurrent cache must hold 36 entries
checks.vllm_generation: vLLM (plugin, the evaluation runner's engine settings): greedy continuations with the top-20 logprobs, re-scored by HF without a cache on prompt + continuation
checks.sensitivity: the same HF cache check on the recurrent model with a deliberately WRONG cache (every logical layer of a block writing one shared entry): it must FAIL the gate, or the check proves nothing and the session stops

engine_validation.metrics: per check: top-1 agreement (the reference's argmax equals the compared path's token) and the mean absolute difference of the compared token's log-probability
engine_validation.gate: PASS iff for hf_cache and vllm_generation alike: recurrent mean |dlogp| <= 3 x control's + 0.02 nats AND recurrent top-1 agreement >= control's - 0.02; AND the shared-cache variant FAILS the hf_cache gate. Fixed before any GPU reading; the thresholds bound bf16 noise relative to the measured control, not an absolute accuracy
engine_validation.not_validated_until_then: the vLLM plugin's import under the vLLM env, torch.compile / CUDA graphs over 36 per-logical-layer Attention modules, the KV-cache sizing, HF / vLLM agreement, the recurrent model's L40S memory and step time (the first four training steps' memory_probe)

diagnostics.role: mechanism diagnostics: never a loss term, never a reason to drop, select or re-tune a run

diagnostics.curves: validation CE and KD at every validation (64 sequences of 8,192 tokens), from the trainer's log
diagnostics.execution: measured seconds per step, peak allocated / reserved memory of the first four steps, evaluation minutes, generated tokens and termination types (natural, degeneration stop, context-limit hit) per mode

initialization_selection.ties_and_unclear: a pooled delta of 0, or seeds that disagree in sign, select KEPT: the simpler initialization (no merge step), whose single-execution control (SOB1's depth arm) is already measured
initialization_selection.incomplete: comparison 1 not complete (a set or a final missing): no selection is written; the binding refuses and the maintainer decides
initialization_selection.independent_of_the_test: the p-value plays no part: a non-significant positive difference in both seeds still selects MERGED, a significant one alone does not decide it
initialization_selection.binding: schedule.py select --write: logs/stages/stage-6/depth_recurrence/plans/init_selection.json from comparison 1's analysis record; schedule.py init-record --write: the recurrent init record over the selected base; plan.py derives variant 2's and 3's units only from a COMPLETE selection and its init record, and refuses any base but the two legal ones

depth_loop.label: recurrent depth, 16 blocks x 36 logical layers

depth_loop_hidden.label: recurrent depth with per-iteration hidden-state distillation

C1.question: alpha-merged initialization vs direct deletion, same structure, same recovery

C2.question: recurrent execution vs single execution from the same initialization

C3.question: adding the per-iteration hidden-state loss to the same recurrent run

analysis_before.primary: per comparison: thinking mode (H-T), static fluid formal core (570 items, 558 independence groups), after recovery, pooled over the two training seeds; each record paired with the other arm's record of the SAME training seed and item (the seeds fix the data order in both arms)
analysis_before.statistic: per comparison (A, B): delta = (1 / (2 x 570)) sum_seeds sum_items (y_X - y_Y); per group g, d_g sums both seeds' differences of the group's items, n_g = 2 |g|
analysis_before.test: TPI1's two-sided group-level paired sign-flip test, B = 100,000, numpy default_rng(20261119)
analysis_before.family: each comparison is its own family, at family-wise alpha 0.05: the thinking-mode test at 0.05; the non-thinking test at 0.05 only if the thinking test rejects (fixed sequence), otherwise non-thinking is descriptive. Each comparison asks about a different intervention, against its own control, decided when its own records are complete; no claim is made that pools or chains them, and none is a gate for another. The 0.05 is each comparison's own family-wise rate: it is NOT a rate controlled over the round's three comparisons together, and no round-wide error rate is claimed
analysis_before.across_comparisons: no adjustment for the per-comparison verdicts (three distinct questions, not one family of exchangeable contrasts -- unlike SOB1's three pairwise arm comparisons, m = 3 is not copied). Reported beside them, once all three exist, as a sensitivity line only: Holm over the three thinking-mode p-values (m = 3)
analysis_before.verdicts: A_BETTER / B_BETTER at p <= 0.05 in the comparison's family, otherwise NOT_DISTINGUISHED (not equivalence)
analysis_before.completeness: a comparison is formal in a mode only when both arms' records of BOTH registered seeds cover all 570 items in that mode; otherwise its deltas and intervals are descriptive and no test is run, never partially pooled
analysis_before.selection_conditioning: C2 and C3 are measured at the initialization comparison 1 chose (schedule.py decide), and that choice read C1's thinking-mode deltas on the SAME eval-set-1 items C2 and C3 are scored on. So C2 estimates the recurrence's effect at the selected initialization, conditional on that selection -- not its effect at an initialization chosen independently of this set; and the MERGED path's control (variant 1) was itself the arm that looked better on these items. A C2 result is reported with this sentence beside it. C3's two arms share the same initialization, so the selection conditions both alike
